BridgeHello.description: Private loader identity. The public Hello payload remains unchanged.

Call_ExecArgs.description: Private adapter payload. Credentials are immutable for this call or subscription.

Call_PrepareRequest.description: Private adapter payload. Credentials are immutable for this call or subscription.

agent.description:
Vessels run the drydock agent from the tools image. Launch reports
success only after the agent's current hello over the SSH reach.

image_routes.description:
How a vessel image reaches this provider, preferred first. A prepare
request that names no route gets the first; one naming another is refused.

platforms.description:
Platforms this provider can run, preferred first. A prepare request
that names none gets the first; one naming another is refused.

suspend_preserves_memory.description: Whether suspend retains running processes/memory, when supported.

Cidr.description: A validated IPv4/IPv6 CIDR, preserving the caller's wire spelling.

ConfiguredProvider.description:
A configured provider is a loader-owned handle, released when the server
drops its trait object (including a rejected configuration transaction).

oneOf.description: `reverse_forwards`: whether the SSH server accepts remote Unix-socket forwards.

Ssh.description: `reverse_forwards`: whether the SSH server accepts remote Unix-socket forwards.

Cost.description:
Currency is explicit, e.g. USD or EUR; the field name fixes no currency.
A missing cost is unknown, whereas an amount of zero is a known zero cost.

CredentialRefresh.description: Delivered in memory over the authenticated host connection; never persisted.

CredentialRegistration.description: How the provider learns the credential for a private registry.

oneOf.description: All ports to this host name; how the provider enforces the name is the provider's choice.

EgressRequest.description: Deny all is the default. Providers must refuse unrepresentable destinations, never widen them.

label.description: Unlabelled resources are listable, inspectable and destroyable.

oneOf.description: The platform the environment runs, when the provider records it.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor to send as `since` on reconnect; resume is exclusive.

oneOf.description: Explicit pause transition, distinct from the more general stopped observation.
The provider explicitly reports destruction without an attributed client request.
A previously known environment is absent from an authoritative complete list.
The provider confirmed deletion requested by the client.

loadable_modules.description: Modules the host can configure, including those not yet loaded.

HostAddress.description: A validated DNS name or IP literal. Schema uses the exact decoder pattern.

ImageRefusal.description: Why a provider cannot take an image. Stable codes for client policy.

oneOf.description: The provider, or the image, offers nothing for this platform.
The image is larger than the provider accepts. `bytes` is a lower bound.

A minted push credential expired before the upload finished. Retrying
mints a new one and resumes from the blobs already uploaded.

ImageRoute.description:
One way a vessel image gets into a provider. Clients choose among declared
routes by these properties and their own policy, never by provider name; a
provider's limits stay properties of its own declaration.

oneOf.description: The host uploads the prepared image into the provider's own registry.

credential_lifetime_seconds.description: How long one minted push credential stays valid, when it expires.

oneOf.description: The provider pulls the base image from a registry it can reach.
The provider builds the image from a recipe the host sends.

smallest_size.description: Smallest supported resource request, used when the caller has no default.

ObserveRecord.description:
Hosts unable to replay emit a snapshot marking the gap. Inventory is complete
only for providers absent from `unavailable_providers`.

unavailable_providers.description:
Providers omitted from this snapshot. Preserve their previous inventory;
omission must not be interpreted as deletion or a billing transition.

ObservedEnvironment.description: Optional provider time travels separately from the environment wire representation.

egress_measured.description:
True only when this call measured the isolation claim; conversion from
a bare Environment conservatively supplies no measurement evidence.

egress_policy.description: Opaque effective-policy identity, present on every cheap observation when supported.

Period.description: RFC 3339 endpoints; start must be <= end (equal endpoints are an empty interval).

Platform.description:
An OCI platform: `os` and `architecture` by OCI names (`linux`, `amd64`,
`arm64`), each 1 to 32 lowercase letters or digits. They become agent build
file and variable names, so decoding refuses anything else.

Port.description: Zero is not a destination port.

PrepareRequest.description:
Preparation is look-up-or-build at the provider: append the tools image's
files under /opt/drydock to the base, preserving its entrypoint, command and
init. tools_digest is the build-selected bootstrap agent OCI index reference.
Its checked-in pin can be older than the host, which upgrades on mismatched
agent hello. Build at the provider where possible, otherwise append its layer;
Upload bootstrap installs those same files under /opt/drydock.
Modules choose their own provider-recorded key including both digests and any
prepare-time constraints (Daytona also includes size); configuration is not a
key. Provision must match the recorded prepared form. See ADR 0070 Vessel tools.

oneOf.description:
Pull access to `image_digest`'s registry, for routes where the host reads
the base image itself. Never sent anywhere else.

Omitted: the provider's first declared platform. Hosts resolve it before
a module prepares, so modules always receive a declared platform.

Omitted: the provider's first declared image route. Hosts resolve it
before a module prepares, so modules always receive a declared route.

platform.description: The platform this prepared form was built for; part of the module's key.

ProtocolError.description: Adaptors never retry. Internal preserves the vendor's raw error text.

oneOf.description: A refusal of the image itself, or of how it was to reach the provider.

provider_error.description: Bounded provider/transport detail, masked for credentials by the host.

oneOf.description: A completed guest command failed, distinct from a vendor/transport outage.

output.description: Vendor-merged guest output. Sensitive diagnostics; never log it.

provider_error.description: Provider explanation, masked for credentials before leaving the host.

ProvisionRequest.description:
Repeated creation with the same label returns the existing environment (200).
Prepared forms belong to one provider; cross-provider use is Refused.

Provisioned.description: Created versus Existing preserves the public 201/200 distinction.

QuotaKey.description:
Scope is data, never an opaque "region/class/resource" string. Missing scope
components mean the provider reports the resource at a broader scope.

reverse_forwards.description:
Whether this SSH server accepts remote (reverse) Unix-socket forwards.
When it does, guest-to-host streams get their own SSH channels; when it
doesn't (Daytona's gateway), they share a link through the local forward.

user.description: May contain a short-lived gateway token; always redact diagnostics.

RegistryCredential.description:
Pull access to one registry. Hosts send it only to the registry that the
reference it accompanies names.

ResourceKind.description:
Initial provider-neutral vocabulary. Adding a resource is a protocol change,
rather than inventing provider-specific encodings inside resource names.

ResourceQuota.description:
The same unit applies to current use and limit. Unknown limits stay unknown.
A vector of these rows keeps structured keys representable as ordinary JSON.

Secret.description:
Secret wire string. Debug output is redacted; serialization deliberately exposes the value.
PartialEq is for wire-value comparisons, NOT constant-time authentication.
Authentication belongs to hosts, which must use constant-time token comparison.
This type does not promise secure erasure of strings or serialization buffers.

SubscriptionRecord.description:
Subscription errors remain typed provider results on the private transport.
These records are not public ObserveRecord events/history.

Timestamp.description: A typed UTC instant, encoded as RFC3339. Equivalent offsets compare equally.

ToolsLayer.description: Where the drydock tools layer joins the base image.

TransitionPhase.description:
Generic phases describe progress, not billing transitions. The host retains
its last stable billing observation until another stable observation arrives.

Update.description: Raw provider facts. No public events, billing transitions or cursors cross this seam.

Usage.description:
Retain the original sandbox-hours-by-size slice. Optional measurements can
reconcile other provider data without fabricating a distribution over sizes.

propertyNames.description:
Initial provider-neutral vocabulary. Adding a resource is a protocol change,
rather than inventing provider-specific encodings inside resource names.

UsageScope.description:
Aggregated usage must say what population it measured. In particular,
organisation totals cannot prove that one suspended environment stopped billing.
Organization and environment IDs are provider-opaque; consumers only compare them.

info.description: Generated from drydock-provider Rust declarations. Loader handles are opaque. Credentials are immutable per call/subscription. Hosts invoke providers without server policy or retries. Managed same-user UDS access uses directory 0700 and socket 0600; no peer UID checks.
